title: Father's secret practices and money
summary: Grateful patient, discovery after death of equipment, father's money, mother's later work.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Something he learned. It's a lot of things.
Growing up in Pointe-Pack. It's a lot of things that he died with, I think, that was secret that he could have helped the world, I think.
Yeah, well there's a lot of, there's a lot, two, I think. A lot of the folk remedies that people use. Yeah.

And that man, he used to lay around on Spruce Street, you know, on Spruce between Eagle and Monroe. And we used to, me and my brother used to pass there, and the man used to just dig in the pocket and give her two and three and five dollars. And say, your daddy saved me, you know. And man, dude, during that time, man, fifty cents to us was a lot of money. You know about two, three, five dollars, man. Yeah. You know? Yeah, man. And I learned that after he died, you know, he died when I was in the Navy, you know, in 1945. When he died, after he died I found out, him and my mother were separated then.

You know. So, she went up there and she found out that he, he had all these things up here where he used to give abortions to women, you know, all this. Oh, really? Yeah, all that. He had all the equipment, the chairs with a little marmalade on and all that.

Wow. He had all that, you know. And he could do anything with a house. He used to wait for those people, you know. A lot of houses he helped prepare down on St. Charles Avenue and the Altman Boulevard. He used to wait for those kind of people, you know. And see, that's another thing I didn't like about him. We around here, you know, like, we look like we're the poorest of the poor. But he used to do all that work, he used to make pretty good money and just carry around in his pocket, you know.
So you think he didn't, he just didn't carry around? No, no. What did your mother, did your mother work at all?

Yeah, he, when they were together, he didn't want her to work, didn't want her to go anywhere, you know, but to church and back, you know. But what happened, what happened was she worked after they separated, you know, but I'll get to that later.
